newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower, stock puzzle continues.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower, stock puzzle continues.

text.p: COMEX copper settled barely lower after a day of nervous trading with little sense of direction as uncertainty was fueled by further reports Wednesday concerning copper stocks, traders said.
World Bureau of Metal Statistics said data suggested there could be 500,000 tonnes of copper in unbonded warehouse in Rotterdam.
And Bloomsbury Minerals Economics said Western exchange stocks may now only account for about a third of the global copper surplus.
Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities said that, nevertheless, exchange stocks were still at six-year lows. "There is essentially a constructive scenario," she added.
December COMEX settled 0.05 cent weaker at 97.90 cents a lb, traded 98.70 to 96.70 cents.
Volume was estimated at 10,000 lots compared to Tuesday's official 13,437 lots.
COMEX stocks on Wednesday rose 174 short tons to 32,374 short tons.
A broker said much of the 150,000-tonne LME stock drawdown since September was due to China replenishing official stocks and to consumers taking back metal they lent to the market.

The rest of the drawdown was largely due to arbitrage deals taking metal from LME warehouses in Long Beach and Hamburg and into COMEX depots in Arizona and Baltimore respectively, the latter route seen by some as an attempt to influence arbitrage premiums, the broker added.
"The market is continuing to look for a surplus that continues to be in the future," he said.
